title: Code Splitting and Lazy Loading
description: Understand code splitting strategies for frontend applications.

options.text: React.lazy() works with server-side rendering out of the box
options.explanation: React.lazy() only works client-side. For SSR, use a library like @loadable/component or React Server Components. React.lazy loads modules via dynamic import() which requires a browser environment.

options.text: Route-based code splitting loads page-specific JavaScript only when the user navigates to that route
options.explanation: By wrapping route components with React.lazy(), each page's code is in a separate chunk loaded on-demand. This dramatically reduces initial bundle size — users only download code for pages they visit.

options.text: More code splitting always results in better performance
options.explanation: Over-splitting creates many tiny chunks, increasing HTTP requests and adding latency from chunk loading. Each split point adds a loading state. Split at meaningful boundaries (routes, heavy libraries), not every component.

options.text: Dynamic import() is synchronous and blocks the main thread
options.explanation: import() is asynchronous — it returns a Promise. The module loads in the background without blocking. This is what enables lazy loading and code splitting.
